primary_sources.title: On Variational Expressions for Quantum Relative Entropies
read_scope: Section I, Lemma 1 and equation (4), including its proof
Bibliographic attribution to Petz in the paragraph immediately before Lemma 1

verified_results.paraphrase: Projectively measured relative entropy equals sup over positive omega of Tr(rho log omega)-log Tr(sigma omega), and also equals sup of Tr(rho log omega)+1-Tr(sigma omega). The second objective is concave in omega.
Optimizing classical KL over general finite POVMs gives the same measured relative entropy as optimizing over rank-one projective measurements.
The paper discusses minimization of quantum or measured relative entropy over convex compact sets of states and the corresponding variational/minimax approach.

exact_relationship_to_local_proof: Our objective Tr(rho log H)+1-Tr(sigma H) is precisely the concave objective in Lemma 1, equation (4), rather than a new variational principle.
Its first-order stationarity condition is Dlog(H)[rho]=sigma because the log Frechet derivative is self-adjoint for the trace inner product. Concavity makes this condition globally sufficient.
The local choice rho=(I+beta Z+gamma X)/2 and H*=I+gamma X explicitly solves that stationarity condition with sigma=(I+beta atanh(gamma)/gamma Z)/2.

Thus the local all-angle upper bound can be obtained directly by applying the established variational theorem to this explicit 2-by-2 stationary point. Our proof spells out the same supporting-hyperplane argument without needing the full measured-relative-entropy theorem.
The physical positivity inequality for sigma, the explicit scalar b*=B atanh(2C)/(2C), and the equal-PSR lower bound specialize the general framework to this oracle design problem.
what_was_not_established: This limited primary-source check did not establish whether the explicit A=1/2 continuous-angle oracle optimum or its closed-form least-favorable null has previously been published.
The inspected article was not verified to state the FaultTune A=1/2 PSR result as an explicit theorem; absence of an explicit statement in these inspected sections is not a novelty finding.

The phrase reverse information projection was not used as a verified theorem label in this source; the precise confirmed link is the measured-relative-entropy variational objective and stationarity condition.
No finite-sample stopping-cost superiority or general-A two-point optimality follows from this literature check.
